text:
Miro Heiskanen left Dallas's game in Washington on Nov. 3 with an upper-body injury and missed five games. He came back in Vegas on Nov. 17 and scored the overtime winner, then opened the scoring in the rematch two nights later. Not a bad way to return.

He is back at 25 to 29 minutes a night, which is the real story for Dallas: the Stars' blue line has been thinned by injuries, and he is the one who carries it. Dallas controls 55.4% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 6.2 points better than without him, and his top speed sits in the 96th percentile by NHL Edge tracking.

The goals won't keep coming at this rate. He has 5 on 1.9 expected, shooting 18% after 6% last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking noted last season that he shoots a lot but not often from the slot. His value is in the minutes and the puck movement, and our range has him at 49 to 72 points with 9 to 18 goals.
